podcast.title: Joining Depeche Mode and Creative Frustration (1982-1991)
podcast.body: Alan Wilder was the last to join Depeche Mode in 1982, serving as a synth player and programmer. By 1991, he grew frustrated as songwriting became almost exclusively Martin Gore's domain, limiting his creative contributions. "He was the last person to join Depeche Mode, signing on in 1982 as a synth player and programmer."

podcast.title: Decision to Leave and Kidney Stone Attack (1992-1994)
podcast.body: Alan Wilder decided during the recording of "Songs of Faith and Devotion" that he would eventually leave Depeche Mode. During a break between the first and second legs of the Devotional Tour, while in South Africa, he suffered an excruciating kidney stone attack. "At some point during the recording process, Alan Wilder decided that when the time was right, he was going to leave the group."

podcast.title: Near-Death Experience (September 1, 1994)
podcast.body: On September 1, 1994, approximately two months after the Devotional Tour concluded, Alan Wilder was driving through the Scottish countryside when an RAF jet fighter trainer almost crashed onto his car, missing him by just over 200 meters. Had his girlfriend not seen the plane approaching and alerted him to pull over into a farm road, his car would have been hit. The two pilots onboard the jet were killed. "Had his girlfriend not seen the plane coming, allowing Alan to pull over into a farm road, his car would have been hit by this plane falling out of the sky."

podcast.title: Departure from Depeche Mode (1995)
podcast.body: Alan Wilder, considered by some to be the "great talent" of Depeche Mode, left the band in 1995 due to what he perceived as an "unsustainable situation." This departure occurred amidst Dave Gahan's severe heroin addiction and Martin Gore's personal struggles, contributing to widespread media speculation about the band's imminent demise. His departure was a major turning point for the band, marking the end of an era. "Alan Wilder que era posiblemente de aquellas. El gran talento de Petchmode que había abandonado el grupo un poco en esa situación insostenible."

podcast.title: Resignation from Depeche Mode (June 1, 1995)
podcast.body: Alan Wilder officially resigned from Depeche Mode on June 1, 1995, after 13 years with the group. His official statement cited increasing dissatisfaction with internal relations, working practices, and a consistent imbalance in the distribution of workload, stating that his input "never received the respect and acknowledgement that it warrants." "On June 1, 1995, almost a year after the tour ended, Alan Wilder resigned from Depeche Mode after serving 13 years with the group."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

podcast.title: Controversial but Beneficial Departure
podcast.body: Alan Wilder's departure sparked significant controversy among Depeche Mode fans, particularly because he held a very clear and defined vision for the band's sound, especially concerning production. While his presence undeniably embodied a crucial part of the band's essence, his leaving ultimately proved beneficial in the long run. It allowed the remaining members to explore new musical horizons, incorporate diverse influences like Trip Hop and Krautrock, and adopt more complex, computerized electronic structures not previously possible under his more synthesiser-focused approach. "Mucha gente yo creo que también ha sido así, a la larga ha sido bastante beneficiosa porque por un lado a la banda le permitió abrirse a nuevos horizontes."

podcast.title: Creative Leader Archetype
podcast.body: Alan Wilder, during his tenure with Depeche Mode, is highlighted as an example of a creative leader in a band, primarily focused on artistic direction and output. "el caso, por ejemplo, de Alan Wilder en la etapa de Petsmoth que ejercía como líder creativo."

podcast.title: Personal Life and Outside Projects (Early 1990s)
podcast.body: Alan Wilder got married and purchased a 30-acre, eight-bedroom estate in the English countryside. He also pursued projects outside Depeche Mode, working with a group called Recoyl and the English Electronic Body Music (EBM) band, Knights of Rab. "He got married and bought a 30-acre eight-bedroom estate in the English countryside."

podcast.title: Post-Depeche Mode Life (Present)
podcast.body: Alan Wilder now lives quietly, having owned a 30-acre, eight-bedroom country estate with his own recording studio. He also possessed a vacation property in Vestfold, Norway. "Alan Wilder is living quietly."

xref.title: Fighter Jet Crash near Alan Wilder (September 1, 1994)
xref.body: On September 1, 1994, while former keyboardist Alan Wilder was driving in the Scottish countryside, a Royal Air Force Tornado fighter jet on a training mission crashed less than 200 yards from his car. Wilder was covered in debris, and the two pilots were killed instantly, an event that profoundly affected his outlook on life. "It was September 1, 1994. Former keyboardist Alan Wilder was driving through the Scottish countryside when on a nowhere, a royal Air Force tornado, a fighter jet on a training mission roared over his car and crashed, less than 200 yards away."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Alan Wilder's Departure (June 1, 1995)
xref.body: On June 1, 1995, Alan Wilder officially left Depeche Mode, unable to tolerate the band's excesses, his limited role in songwriting, and his bandmates. The earlier fighter plane crash incident also contributed to his reassessment of his life and priorities. "On June 1st, 1995, Alan Wilder made it official. He could not take it anymore. He could not stand the excess. He could not stand not being able to write more of the music. And he could not stand any of his bandmates."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Long-Term Recovery and Current Status (1997-Present)
xref.body: Depeche Mode eventually overcame the tumultuous period between 1991 and 1997. Dave Gahan and Martin Gore are now sober, and Alan Wilder is living a quiet life. While Andy Fletcher died in 2022, Martin Gore and Dave Gahan continue to record and tour together, showing intent to move forward almost 50 years after the band's formation. "The good news is that the Pesh mode eventually came out on the other side of all things that happened between 1991 and 1997."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Alan Wilder's Departure
xref.body: Following the difficult 1993-94 Devotional Tour and its associated problems within the band, Alan Wilder made the decision to quit Depeche Mode permanently. "Alan Wilder quit the band forever."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Decadent Tour Staff and Incidents
xref.body: The "Songs of Faith and Devotion" tour employed approximately 100 individuals, including a dedicated full-time psychiatrist and a staff member specifically tasked with procuring drugs. During this tour, several band members experienced severe issues: Martin Gore suffered two grand mal seizures and numerous panic attacks, Andrew Fletcher endured a mental breakdown so severe that doctors initially suspected a brain tumor, and keyboardist Alan Wilder ultimately quit the band. "The tour employed a hundred people, including a full-time psychiatrist and a guy whose job it was to buy drugs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early 90s Struggles
xref.body: In the early 1990s, Depeche Mode was in a "very bad place" largely due to extensive drug and alcohol use. Martin Gore suffered severe seizures, leading doctors to suspect a brain tumor. Andy Fletcher (Fletch) experienced debilitating panic attacks, and keyboardist Alan Wilder quit the band due to the stress. Singer Dave Gahan was heavily addicted to heroin and cocaine. "In the early 90s, Depeche Mode was in a very bad place. Thanks to lots and lots and lots of drugs and alcohol."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Tour Health Crisis (Devotional Tour Aftermath)
xref.body: The aftermath of the Devotional Tour saw several band members facing severe health issues: Alan Wilder was diagnosed with kidney and gall stones during the South African leg; Andrew Fletcher nearly suffered a nervous breakdown and left the tour for treatment after his sister died of stomach cancer; Martin Gore experienced a grand mal seizure during a business meeting due to excessive drugs and alcohol; and Dave Gahan's severe drug use led to extreme weight loss (under 100 pounds) and an incident where he bit a journalist on the neck. "During the South African leg, Alan Wilder was diagnosed with kidney stones and then gall stones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rejected "Music for the Masses" Cover
xref.body: An alternative cover for Depeche Mode's *Music for the Masses* was created, featuring a stylized megaphone in a white and orange motif with drawn sound waves. Approximately 135 copies were prepared for distribution to stores before the band and label had a change of heart, recalling and destroying nearly all of them. About a dozen copies remained with retailers. In 2011, keyboardist Alan Wilder auctioned off his copy, fetching around $4,000, and it is now considered extremely rare, with Discogs reporting no sales of this version. "About 135 copies were prepared for shipping to stores, but then the band and the label had a change of heart and had all those copies recalled."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Songwriting Dominance and Personal Challenges (Early 1990s)
xref.body: Martin Gore became the sole songwriter for Depeche Mode, which created tension with Alan Wilder. He claimed to be autistic and indulged heavily in partying and drinking, often withdrawing into video games like "Sonic the Hedgehog." Becoming a father for the first time in June 1991 added further stress. "He wanted to contribute more as a songwriter, but that had pretty much become the sole domain of Martin Gore."
